title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. X/S is a smooth relative curve, ω = Ω^1_{X/S}, and P = P(P^1_{X/S}(ω)) (or a twist P(P^1(Ω)) for an invertible Ω) is the P^1-bundle of 1-jets. A first-order differential operator D: ω → L gives a section σ' of P. Its symbol γ_0 ∈ Γ(L⊗ω^{-2}) is defined by D(fω) − fD(ω) = γ_0(ω·df). On the previous page Grothendieck shows that σ' meets the canonical section σ (the sub-line ω^2 ⊂ P^1(ω)) exactly at the zeros of γ_0, the 'degeneracy points' of D. On the open set U where D is non-degenerate, σ' is transverse to σ. There it determines a unique projective connection (a PGL_2-connection on P, an sl_2-oper / indigenous structure in Gunning's sense) for which σ' is horizontal.

This page states the extension criterion. A projective connection on all of X making σ' horizontal exists if and only if two conditions hold:
(a) U is fibrewise dense;
(b) the connection defined on U extends regularly across the degeneracy points. The extension is then unique.

Condition (b) is purely local at each degeneracy point. In a local coordinate t, the connection on U is described by an invariant λ (on the next page λ_t = b/a, where D(f dt) = a f' + b). The quadratic differential coming from the Riccati expression λ^2 + dλ/dt must have no pole where λ has one. Therefore λ has at most a simple pole, with a fixed residue and a fixed constant term (the 'partie principale polaire à l'ordre 1 près' is determined).

Geometric reformulation. Along σ there is a canonical field of second-order contact elements transverse to σ. The sections σ' of P coming from a global projective connection with σ' horizontal (unique when it exists) are exactly those whose 2-jet, at each intersection point with σ, agrees with this field.

The NB generalizes the setup. The same picture holds whenever P^1(Ω) is replaced by any extension of an invertible Ω by Ω⊗ω (next page).

In modern terms: a section of an indigenous P^1-bundle is horizontal for some oper exactly when its tangency points with the Hodge/canonical section are 'apparent' branch points. These are simple branch points of a branched projective structure, which correspond to apparent singularities of the associated Fuchsian equation: exponent difference 2 and no logarithmic term.
errors: Normalization inconsistency across pages. Here the condition is phrased via λ^2 + dλ/dt, which forces residue 1 for a simple pole: (c^2 − c)/t^2 = 0 gives c ∈ {0,1}, and then the constant term must vanish. The next page states the residue as 2 with no constant term, which corresponds to λ^2/2 + λ' or to a different choice of invariant. This is a harmless convention change, not a substantive error.
The parenthetical '(ceci [vient] que λ^2 + dλ/dt n'a pas de pôle en un pt où λ en a un !)' must be read as the requirement being imposed, not as a general claim. As a general claim it is false.
Condition (a) as written is somewhat loose. Fibrewise density of U is needed for the uniqueness and extension argument; also, a and b must not vanish simultaneously (next page).

ideas.what: First-order differential operator D: ω→L viewed as a section σ' of the P^1-bundle P(P^1_{X/S}(ω)); its degeneracy points are the intersections with the canonical section σ.
ideas.modern_name: Sections of indigenous/oper P^1-bundles; Gunning's indigenous bundles with the Hodge section

ideas.what: Unique projective connection making a transverse section horizontal on the non-degenerate locus.
ideas.modern_name: Projective structure induced by a local coordinate / developing map (oper ↔ section transverse to the Hodge filtration)

ideas.what: Local criterion for extension across degeneracy points: λ has a simple pole with prescribed residue and no constant term; equivalently, at each intersection point the 2-jet of σ' agrees with a canonical field of second-order contact elements along σ.
ideas.modern_name: Apparent singularities / simple branch points of branched projective structures (exponent difference 2, no logarithm)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mandelbaum (1972–73); Gallo–Kapovich–Marden (2000); classical Fuchs theory of apparent singularities

ideas.what: Generalization to arbitrary extensions of an invertible Ω by Ω⊗ω (not only the jet bundle).
ideas.modern_name: PGL_2-opers on arbitrary rank-2 extensions; relative/arithmetic opers

missed.claim: Grothendieck gives a relative, algebraic (over an arbitrary base S, in a context alongside Gauss–Manin/Cartier) characterization of which sections of the jet P^1-bundle are horizontal for a projective connection. The characterization is a geometric 2-jet tangency condition with a canonical field of second-order contact elements along the canonical section. This is a coordinate-free formulation of the apparent-singularity / simple-branch-point condition for branched projective structures, made around 1972. That is contemporaneous with Mandelbaum and predates the oper language.
missed.quote: les sections σ' de P ... lesquelles il y a une connexion projective de X rendant σ' horizontale (laquelle sera unique) sont celles qui, en un pt d'intersection avec σ, ont comme pt d'ordre 2 celui du champ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The 'canonical field of 2-jets along the Hodge section' formulation is a clean intrinsic description of branched opers (opers with apparent singularities). These now appear in geometric Langlands (Frenkel–Gaitsgory 'opers with regular singularities and trivial monodromy') and in p-adic/char-p work (Mochizuki, dormant opers). Historically it shows Grothendieck working on indigenous-bundle geometry in the relative setting. The ideas themselves are, however, known in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct and neat local criterion, phrased geometrically via 2-jets along the canonical section and in a relative algebraic setting, for branched projective structures / opers with apparent singularities. The mathematics is known (Fuchsian apparent singularities, Mandelbaum, later opers), so the novelty is mainly historical: Grothendieck pursuing indigenous-bundle and oper geometry around 1972, unpublished.
transcription_corrections: Line 1–3: likely 'Pour que la section σ' de P soit horizontale pour une conn. projective convenable (il faut et il suffit) que l'ouvert U des pts où D est non dég. soit dense sur chaque fibre de X sur S et b) que la section qu'on vient de définir sur U se prolonge...'
'Torsion [?] Connexion sans ω^2' is uncertain; possibly 'Trouver Connexions sans ω^2', i.e. a projective connection (a connection modulo ω^2) 'doit vérifier en section régulière sur tout X'.
'd'éléments de section d'ordre 2' is probably 'd'éléments de courbe (or de contact) d'ordre 2 transverses à σ'.
'sections σ' de P^1_{U/S}' is probably 'sections σ' de P' (the superscript is an inserted annotation).
